It all depends how seriously you want to take it. If you 100% want to get really good at drawing things well, like it's one of the big things you want as a hobby or profession, then you should learn stuff from the ground-up starting with basic shapes, learning perspective and geometry, learning basic shading techniques so you can help visualise things as 3D, and then learning anatomy (of humans and animals) so you can draw real and imaginary things in a realistic fashion. Then, when you understand how things are physically built, you can start to get stylized and use shortcuts to make things look more how you want them. Anime in particular is like 80% shortcuts, which leads to a nice style that's somehow both sharp and smooth that a lot of people grow fond of. But to draw it well, and to be a good artist, you've got to understand how to do it without the shortcuts, so you can do the shortcuts correctly.
Of course if you just want to draw for fun, this is still a perfectly good strategy, but you might end up going through it a lot faster and doing a lot less practice, just so you understand the basics and can slowly figure them out while you have fun drawing random things. Also keep in mind you'll at some point find a particular kind of thing you're good at drawing. I am terrible at drawing organic shapes, for example, but I can draw weapons pretty well for my skill level.

Take a sketching and/or figure drawing class at your local community college - I've always been naturally decent at drawing but you will learn a lot that will get into your subconscious and muscle memory for drawing well on the fly!
